text: A sprinter keeps the same force but applies it through a longer perpendicular moment arm. What changes most directly?
options: The torque about the joint increases
The athlete's body mass decreases
The movement's linear speed becomes zero
The joint loses all external force
explanation: Torque equals force multiplied by the perpendicular moment arm. With force unchanged, a longer moment arm produces more torque.

text: A 20-second maximal effort is repeated after a short recovery. Which process is especially important for restoring the immediate high-power energy supply between efforts?
options: Conversion of all lactate into fat
Oxidative phosphocreatine resynthesis
Complete replacement of muscle protein
Suppression of mitochondrial respiration
explanation: Oxidative metabolism helps resynthesise phosphocreatine during recovery, supporting repeated high-power efforts.

text: Which macronutrient provides approximately 9 kilocalories per gram and has an important role in cell membranes and hormone production?
options: Protein
Carbohydrate
Fat
Water
explanation: Fat provides about 9 kilocalories per gram and is also needed for cell structures and several physiological functions.

text: An athlete performs well when moderately alert but makes rushed decisions when highly anxious. Which principle best explains this observation?
options: Arousal has no relationship to performance
All athletes have the same ideal arousal level
High arousal always improves fine motor skill
The optimal arousal zone depends on the task and athlete
explanation: The relationship between arousal and performance is individual and task-dependent; excessive arousal can impair decision-making.

text: Which rehabilitation sequence best reflects a criteria-based progression after a sports injury?
options: Protect the tissue, restore capacity, add sport demands, then reassess
Return to competition, then begin strengthening if symptoms persist
Use passive treatment only until the calendar clearance date
Test maximal sport speed before checking basic movement quality
explanation: Rehabilitation progressively restores tissue capacity and function before exposing the athlete to the demands of competition.

text: Which training principle means that an adaptation is most specific to the movement, intensity and energy demand practised?
options: Variation
Specificity
Reversibility
Randomisation
explanation: Specificity means that training adaptations reflect the characteristics of the training stimulus.

text: Why can body mass index misclassify a muscular athlete as having excess adiposity?
options: It measures only resting heart rate
It is calculated from skinfold thickness alone
It cannot distinguish lean mass from fat mass
It directly measures visceral fat volume
explanation: Body mass index uses mass and height, so it does not identify how much of the mass is muscle, bone or adipose tissue.

text: During a single-leg landing, which change generally makes balance more difficult?
options: Widening the base of support
Lowering the centre of mass
Keeping the centre of mass over the base
Raising the centre of mass while narrowing the base
explanation: A higher centre of mass and a narrower base reduce the margin for maintaining the centre of mass within the base of support.

text: Which stored substrate is especially important for repeated high-intensity exercise and can become limiting when carbohydrate availability is low?
options: Muscle glycogen
Bone collagen
Dietary fibre
Plasma albumin
explanation: Muscle glycogen supports glycolytic and oxidative carbohydrate use during exercise, particularly at higher intensities.

text: A performance analyst notices that a workload change coincided with poor sleep and new pain. What is the most useful team response?
options: Ask only the coach to decide whether the athlete is fit
Combine training, health, recovery and athlete-reported information
Ignore subjective information because it is not numerical
Change every training variable at the same time
explanation: Performance decisions improve when objective load data are interpreted with health, recovery and athlete context by the relevant team.

text: A test gives nearly the same result on repeated trials but does not measure the performance quality it claims to measure. How should it be described?
options: Sensitive but not standardised
Valid but completely unreliable
Reliable but not valid for that purpose
Specific but not repeatable
explanation: Reliability concerns consistency; validity concerns whether the test measures the intended construct.

text: Which change most improves standardisation when a team repeats a jump test during a season?
options: Allowing each tester to give different instructions
Changing footwear at every testing session
Testing only on days when the result is expected to improve
Using the same warm-up, instructions, equipment and rest period
explanation: Keeping procedures, equipment, instructions and rest consistent reduces avoidable measurement variation.

text: A change smaller than the test's typical measurement error is observed after training. What is the safest interpretation?
options: The change may be noise and should be interpreted cautiously
The test has proven perfect validity
The result should replace all other assessments
The athlete definitely improved clinically
explanation: A result must exceed expected measurement error, or be supported by other evidence, before a real change is inferred.

text: An athlete reports unusual fatigue before a maximal test despite a normal previous score. What is the best immediate decision?
options: Proceed without recording the fatigue because the test is scheduled
Record the context and consider postponing or modifying the test
Increase the test intensity to reveal the problem
Average the result with the athlete's best score
explanation: Readiness, safety and interpretation depend on context. A symptomatic athlete may need a modified or deferred test rather than a forced maximal effort.

text: A team compares high-speed running from two devices with different sampling rates. What is the main concern?
options: Higher sampling always proves the athlete ran farther
Running speed is never measurable outside a laboratory
Device settings can affect the measured value and comparability
The result is independent of device placement
explanation: Sampling rate, device model, placement and processing methods can affect GPS-derived distance and speed measures.

text: Which sensor primarily detects linear acceleration along its measurement axes?
options: Barometer
Electrocardiograph
Thermistor
Accelerometer
explanation: An accelerometer measures acceleration. Wearable inertial systems may combine it with gyroscopes and magnetometers.

text: A drop in an athlete's morning heart-rate variability is recorded once after a late flight. What is the best interpretation?
options: It is a context-dependent signal that needs a trend and other data
It proves the athlete is injured
It proves overtraining syndrome
It should automatically trigger maximal training
explanation: Heart-rate variability is influenced by sleep, travel, illness, stress and measurement conditions; one reading is not diagnostic.

text: What does a force platform measure most directly during a countermovement jump?
options: Bone mineral density
The force exerted on the platform over time
Subjective confidence
Hormone concentration
explanation: A force platform records force against time, from which variables such as impulse, peak force and rate of force development may be derived.

text: A small group has one extremely high sprint-load value. Which measure is usually less affected by that outlier?
options: Standard deviation only
Mean
Median
Maximum
explanation: The median is the middle ordered value and is generally less influenced by an extreme observation than the mean.

text: A 95% confidence interval around a group mean is narrow. What does that most directly suggest?
options: Every athlete had exactly the mean value
There was no measurement error at all
The intervention is automatically clinically important
The estimate is relatively precise in that sample
explanation: A narrower interval indicates greater precision of the estimated mean, but it does not by itself establish clinical importance or zero error.

text: When a screening test is used to rule out a serious condition, which test characteristic is especially valuable when negative?
options: High sensitivity
High false-positive rate
Low specificity
A large standard deviation
explanation: A highly sensitive test has few false negatives, so a negative result is more useful for ruling out a condition when applied appropriately.

text: A performance change is statistically significant but smaller than the team's pre-defined smallest worthwhile change. What should the analyst report?
options: It is definitely important to selection decisions
Statistical evidence exists, but practical importance may be limited
It proves the test is unreliable
The p-value should be ignored completely
explanation: Statistical significance and practical or sporting importance are related but different judgements.

text: What is the usual aim of a pre-competition taper?
options: Increase volume until the day of competition
Stop all movement for several weeks
Reduce training volume while retaining relevant intensity
Replace sport practice with passive treatment only
explanation: Tapering reduces accumulated fatigue while preserving fitness through an appropriate amount of intensity and specificity.

text: Which recovery action is most fundamental when an athlete has repeatedly shortened sleep because of late training?
options: Add a new supplement immediately
Ignore sleep because only heart rate matters
Use maximal exercise to induce deeper fatigue
Correct the schedule and protect adequate regular sleep
explanation: Training-dose and sleep regularity are foundational recovery levers; passive tools cannot reliably compensate for chronic sleep restriction.

text: Which change is an expected adaptation to repeated, appropriately dosed heat exposure?
options: Earlier and more effective sweating with improved heat tolerance
Reduced plasma volume in every athlete
Earlier complete cessation of sweating
Loss of all cardiovascular strain during exercise
explanation: Heat acclimatisation can improve sweating response, plasma volume and cardiovascular stability, but it does not remove all heat stress.

text: A sudden large increase in high-speed running is followed by pain. Which monitoring principle is most appropriate?
options: Use one load number to predict injury with certainty
Interpret load changes with symptoms, capacity, recovery and context
Increase the next session to build toughness
Ignore external load if the athlete completed the session
explanation: Load is one part of risk and readiness. Interpretation should include exposure history, tissue capacity, recovery and symptoms.

text: After travelling east across several time zones, what adjustment is generally required by the athlete's body clock?
options: No adjustment because travel does not affect circadian timing
A phase delay only, regardless of the competition time
A phase advance, supported by a planned sleep and light schedule
Continuous daytime sleeping until symptoms disappear
explanation: Eastward travel usually requires advancing the circadian phase. The actual light and sleep plan should match the itinerary.

text: Which finding should increase concern about low energy availability in an athlete?
options: Improved recovery and stable health markers
A normal result on one isolated fitness test
A single day of high carbohydrate intake
Persistent fatigue, recurrent injury and menstrual or endocrine disturbance
explanation: Low energy availability can affect multiple systems, including bone, endocrine, immune and reproductive health, and should be assessed holistically.

text: A coach asks for the athlete's complete medical record. What is the most ethical response?
options: Share only necessary information with consent and an appropriate purpose
Refuse every form of communication with the team
Send everything because the coach controls selection
Post the record in the team communication group
explanation: Confidentiality requires limiting disclosure to necessary information, with informed consent and a legitimate professional purpose.

text: An athlete discloses repeated humiliating messages from a staff member. What should be the first professional priority?
options: Ask the athlete to confront the staff member alone
Protect the athlete, document the concern and follow the safeguarding pathway
Delete the messages to avoid reputational harm
Wait until the season ends before recording it
explanation: A safeguarding concern should be taken seriously, recorded factually, escalated through the appropriate process and managed with attention to immediate safety.

text: Before an athlete uses a new supplement, which sequence is the most responsible?
options: Take it first and check the label only if a test is scheduled
Assume natural products cannot contain prohibited substances
Check need, evidence, contamination risk and anti-doping status before use
Use a teammate's product because it worked for them
explanation: Supplements can be contaminated or mislabelled. Need, evidence, product quality and anti-doping risk should be considered before use.

text: At altitude, an athlete develops worsening headache, confusion and breathlessness at rest. What is the safest response?
options: Continue hard training to accelerate adaptation
Treat it as ordinary delayed-onset muscle soreness
Give a stimulant and keep the athlete alone
Stop the exposure and arrange urgent medical assessment
explanation: Worsening neurological or respiratory symptoms at altitude are red flags and require removal from risk and urgent medical evaluation.

text: Which body is primarily responsible for the technical rules of a particular Olympic sport?
options: The International Federation for that sport
The host organising committee
The National Olympic Committee of the host country
The Olympic village medical team
explanation: The relevant International Federation governs the technical rules and competition regulations of its sport.

text: Which city hosted the first Asian Games in 1951?
options: Tokyo
New Delhi
Seoul
Bangkok
explanation: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi in 1951.

text: The main purpose of the Target Olympic Podium Scheme is to support which group?
options: Only retired athletes seeking employment
All school students irrespective of sporting pathway
Athletes with realistic potential for Olympic and major-games success
Only officials responsible for stadium construction
explanation: The Target Olympic Podium Scheme supports identified elite athletes and their preparation for major international competition.

text: Which activity best fits the development focus of the Khelo India programme?
options: Selecting the host city for the Olympic Games
Replacing every National Sports Federation's technical rules
Issuing anti-doping sanctions after a positive test
Talent identification, competitions and broad sports participation
explanation: Khelo India includes participation, competitions, talent development and sports infrastructure or centre-based initiatives.

text: Why are whereabouts requirements used in anti-doping programmes?
options: To make unannounced testing possible for athletes in a testing pool
To allow athletes to choose whether a sample is tested
To replace all education about prohibited substances
To guarantee that an athlete will never be tested in competition
explanation: Whereabouts information supports effective no-advance-notice testing for athletes subject to the applicable requirements.

text: An athlete needs a prohibited medicine for a diagnosed condition. What should the athlete do?
options: Stop all medical care and self-treat with supplements
Apply for a therapeutic use exemption when the criteria and timing require it
Assume a doctor's prescription automatically removes anti-doping responsibility
Wait for a positive test before mentioning the medicine
explanation: A prescription does not automatically authorise a prohibited substance in sport. The athlete and medical team must follow the therapeutic use exemption process.

text: Which organisation governs the World Athletics Championships?
options: International Basketball Federation
International Cricket Council
World Athletics
Commonwealth Sport
explanation: World Athletics is the international governing body associated with the World Athletics Championships.

text: A selector is asked to evaluate an athlete who is a close family member. What is the most ethical action?
options: Keep the relationship secret if the athlete is performing well
Ask the athlete to decide whether the conflict matters
Score the athlete first and disclose it only if challenged
Disclose the conflict and follow the independent selection process
explanation: Disclosure and appropriate management of a conflict protect fairness, transparency and trust in selection decisions.

text: Which rotator-cuff muscle is most associated with initiating shoulder abduction?
options: Supraspinatus
Subscapularis
Teres major
Pectoralis minor
explanation: Supraspinatus assists the initial phase of shoulder abduction before the deltoid contributes more strongly.

text: Weakness of ankle dorsiflexion after injury near the fibular neck most strongly suggests involvement of which nerve?
options: Tibial nerve
Common fibular nerve
Femoral nerve
Obturator nerve
explanation: The common fibular nerve is vulnerable near the fibular neck and contributes through its deep branch to ankle dorsiflexion.

text: The anterior cruciate ligament primarily limits which motion of the tibia relative to the femur?
options: Posterior translation
Medial rotation only
Anterior translation
Lateral translation only
explanation: The anterior cruciate ligament is a major restraint to anterior tibial translation and contributes to rotational stability.

text: Which muscle is a prime contributor to knee extension?
options: Biceps femoris
Soleus
Popliteus
Quadriceps femoris
explanation: The quadriceps femoris group extends the knee; the rectus femoris also crosses the hip.

text: A posterolateral lumbar disc protrusion most commonly threatens which structure in the spinal canal?
options: The descending nerve root below the disc
The exiting nerve root at the same level only
The femoral artery in the groin
The brachial plexus
explanation: A posterolateral lumbar disc lesion commonly affects the traversing or descending nerve root below the disc level.

text: During progressive aerobic exercise, cardiac output rises mainly because of increases in which two variables?
options: Blood viscosity and residual volume
Heart rate and stroke volume
Respiratory dead space and blood pressure only
Bone density and venous valve stiffness
explanation: Cardiac output equals heart rate multiplied by stroke volume, and both generally contribute during graded exercise.

text: According to the Fick principle, oxygen consumption equals cardiac output multiplied by what?
options: Inspiratory reserve volume
Respiratory exchange ratio
Arterial-venous oxygen difference
Blood lactate concentration
explanation: The Fick equation is VO2 = cardiac output × arterial-venous oxygen difference.

text: What does a lactate threshold test attempt to identify during incremental exercise?
options: The exact time when all aerobic metabolism stops
The number of motor units in one muscle
The athlete's maximum bone length
The exercise intensity at which lactate begins accumulating disproportionately
explanation: Threshold concepts describe a rise in blood lactate relative to workload; they do not mean aerobic metabolism has stopped.

text: During intense exercise, ventilation may rise disproportionately as acidity increases. Which response helps compensate?
options: Increased carbon dioxide exhalation
Complete closure of the airways
Reduced carbon dioxide removal
Suppression of respiratory drive
explanation: Increased ventilation helps remove carbon dioxide and supports buffering of the increased acid load during intense exercise.

text: Delayed-onset muscle soreness is most strongly associated with which type of unfamiliar loading?
options: Repeated low-load breathing
Unaccustomed eccentric exercise
Passive joint positioning only
A single brief isometric contraction
explanation: Unaccustomed eccentric exercise is a common trigger for delayed-onset muscle soreness, which usually develops hours after exercise.

text: A conventional sensory-level transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation setting is primarily intended to influence pain through which mechanism?
options: Thermal destruction of the peripheral nerve
Complete denervation of the painful muscle
Activation of large sensory afferents and spinal gating
Permanent shortening of the tendon
explanation: Conventional sensory-level stimulation is commonly explained through activation of large-diameter sensory afferents and modulation of nociceptive transmission.

text: The principal rehabilitation use of neuromuscular electrical stimulation after inhibition-related weakness is to assist which goal?
options: Replacing all voluntary exercise permanently
Diagnosing a meniscal tear without examination
Increasing bone length in an adult
Facilitating muscle contraction while voluntary control is rebuilt
explanation: Neuromuscular stimulation can assist contraction and training when voluntary activation is limited, but it does not replace progressive active rehabilitation.

text: Compared with a higher frequency therapeutic ultrasound beam, a lower frequency beam generally penetrates which way?
options: More deeply
Less deeply
Only through bone
Only across the skin surface
explanation: Lower ultrasound frequencies are generally selected for greater depth, while higher frequencies are used for more superficial tissues.

text: Before applying electrical stimulation, which action is most important when the athlete reports an implanted electronic device?
options: Increase intensity until the athlete feels a strong contraction
Check the device, treatment area and current safety guidance before proceeding
Ignore it if the skin sensation is normal
Place electrodes directly over the implant to test tolerance
explanation: Implanted electronic devices require a specific safety assessment and may contraindicate or restrict electrical stimulation depending on device and location.

subtopic: Open and closed kinetic chain exercise
text: Which exercise is an example of a closed kinetic chain task for the lower limb?
options: Seated knee extension with the foot free
Straight-leg raise in supine
Standing squat with the feet fixed to the floor
Open-chain ankle dorsiflexion
explanation: In a closed kinetic chain task, the distal segment is fixed or weight-bearing, as in a squat.

text: An athlete with load-related tendinopathy tolerates slow strengthening without a symptom flare the next day. What is the most appropriate progression principle?
options: Use passive modalities as the only intervention
Stop all loading until the tendon is pain-free for a month
Change to random maximal jumps immediately
Increase load or complexity gradually while monitoring response
explanation: Tendon rehabilitation usually progresses exposure to load and function according to symptoms, capacity and sport demands.

text: The diagonal patterns used in proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation are intended to resemble which type of movement?
options: Functional, multijoint movement patterns
Only isolated movement at one joint
Passive movement with no sensory input
A purely cardiovascular endurance test
explanation: Proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation uses diagonal, spiral and multijoint patterns to facilitate coordinated functional movement.

text: A rehabilitation exercise is no longer challenging and produces no meaningful response. Which change best reflects progressive overload?
options: Remove all rest and ignore technique
Increase an appropriate training variable while preserving quality
Repeat exactly the same dose forever
Replace strength work with complete immobilisation
explanation: Progressive overload changes a relevant dose variable such as resistance, volume, speed or complexity while maintaining safe technique and recovery.

text: Which progression most increases the challenge of a stable-surface balance task?
options: Perform it seated with both feet supported
Widen the base and add hand support
Add visual or cognitive challenge while maintaining safety
Remove all supervision from the first attempt
explanation: Reducing visual information or adding a task can increase balance demand, but progression must remain safe and appropriate to the athlete.

text: Impulse is calculated as force multiplied by what quantity?
options: Distance only
Joint angle
Body mass squared
Time
explanation: Impulse equals force multiplied by the time over which it acts and represents a change in momentum.

text: During landing, the ground reaction force is best understood as which force?
options: The force exerted by the ground on the athlete
The force produced only by the athlete's muscles
The athlete's internal joint torque without external contact
The force of gravity removed from the body
explanation: Ground reaction force is the external force exerted by the ground on the body in response to contact.

text: Holding a dumbbell farther from the elbow increases the external elbow torque mainly because it increases which variable?
options: The muscle's cross-sectional area
The perpendicular moment arm of the load
The athlete's oxygen saturation
The joint's cartilage thickness
explanation: External torque depends on the load and its perpendicular distance from the joint axis.

text: A complete gait cycle is conventionally described from one event to which repeated event?
options: The end of the next training session
The next event on the opposite arm
The same event on the same limb
The athlete's maximum heart rate
explanation: A gait cycle is measured from one occurrence of a reference event, such as initial contact, to the next occurrence on the same limb.

text: Excessive dynamic knee valgus during a single-leg squat describes a combination that commonly includes which movement pattern?
options: Spinal extension with elbow flexion
Knee flexion with hip external rotation only
Ankle inversion with hip abduction only
Knee abduction with hip adduction and internal rotation
explanation: Dynamic valgus is a movement pattern rather than a single joint motion and often includes hip adduction/internal rotation with knee medial displacement.

text: A sprinter uses the cue “tall and quick” before each start. This is best classified as which psychological skill?
options: Structured self-talk
External locus of control
Avoidance conditioning
Random attentional drift
explanation: A brief intentional cue is a form of self-talk used to direct attention and support execution.

text: Worrying about selection and feeling tense before competition represent which two common dimensions of anxiety?
options: Strength and power
Cognitive and somatic anxiety
Intrinsic and extrinsic fatigue
Validity and reliability
explanation: Cognitive anxiety involves worry or negative thoughts, while somatic anxiety involves perceived physiological activation and tension.

text: Why should training loads for adolescents be individualised rather than based only on chronological age?
options: Chronological age predicts exact tissue capacity
Young athletes cannot adapt to any resistance exercise
Maturation and training history vary between athletes of the same age
Growth makes all injury prevention unnecessary
explanation: Growth, maturation, training history, skill and health status differ among adolescents, so load should be individualised and monitored.

text: The Ottawa ankle rules are primarily used to help decide whether which investigation may be indicated after an acute ankle injury?
options: An electroencephalogram
A shoulder ultrasound
A pulmonary function test
A bone radiograph
explanation: The Ottawa ankle rules help identify patients who may need ankle or foot radiographs after acute injury; they do not replace clinical judgement.

text: The Lachman test is primarily used to assess which structure?
options: Anterior cruciate ligament
Posterior cruciate ligament
Medial collateral ligament only
Achilles tendon
explanation: The Lachman test assesses anterior translation and the integrity of the anterior cruciate ligament.

text: Pain or weakness during resisted shoulder abduction with the arm in the scapular plane may suggest involvement of which region?
options: The plantar fascia
The rotator cuff
The Achilles tendon
The lumbar disc
explanation: Resisted abduction in the scapular plane loads the shoulder abductors, including the supraspinatus and deltoid, and may provoke rotator-cuff symptoms.

text: Which presentation in an athlete with low-back pain requires urgent escalation rather than routine exercise progression?
options: Mild stiffness after a new training week
Pain that improves with a warm-up
New saddle anaesthesia with bladder disturbance
Muscle soreness after familiar strengthening
explanation: Saddle anaesthesia and bladder disturbance raise concern for serious neurological compromise and require urgent medical assessment.

text: What is the main purpose of a differential diagnosis in sports physiotherapy?
options: To list every possible disease without testing
To replace medical referral in every case
To avoid asking about the athlete's goals
To compare plausible explanations and choose safe next steps
explanation: Differential diagnosis organises plausible explanations, guides examination and helps identify when referral or urgent care is required.

text: An athlete has suspected concussion but wants to continue because symptoms are mild. What is the appropriate immediate action?
options: Remove the athlete from play for assessment and do not allow same-day return without the appropriate process
Allow play if the athlete signs a waiver
Give analgesia and test only after the match
Ask a teammate to monitor the athlete while play continues
explanation: Suspected concussion requires removal from play, assessment and a graduated, medically supervised return-to-sport process.

text: Why should high-speed running be reintroduced progressively during hamstring rehabilitation?
options: It prevents all muscle contraction during healing
It exposes the muscle to the sport-specific demand in a controlled way
It proves imaging is no longer needed in any case
It makes strength testing unnecessary
explanation: Progressive running exposure restores tolerance to the speed and lengthening demands that may be relevant to the athlete's sport.

text: An athlete is confused, collapses during hot exercise and has very hot skin. What is the priority?
options: Delay treatment until a laboratory test confirms the diagnosis
Give a large amount of concentrated sports drink and return to play
Begin immediate whole-body cooling while activating emergency care
Massage the legs and keep the athlete in the sun
explanation: Suspected exertional heat stroke is a medical emergency. Rapid cooling and emergency activation should not wait for laboratory confirmation.

text: During a long flight after recent lower-limb surgery, which advice is most appropriate as part of the medical plan?
options: Remain completely immobile throughout the flight
Use an unprescribed anticoagulant from a teammate
Assume compression is safe for every patient without assessment
Discuss individual risk, move regularly and follow the treating clinician's plan
explanation: Travel after surgery requires individual risk assessment and a clinician-led plan; movement and other measures should be appropriate to the person.

text: An athlete's pain rises after a training spike but settles when the next session is reduced. What does this pattern support?
options: A need to match load progression to current capacity and response
Proof that all exercise is harmful
A diagnosis based only on the pain score
A reason to increase the load immediately
explanation: Symptoms can inform load adjustment, but the pattern should be interpreted with examination, capacity and sport demands rather than used as a diagnosis alone.

text: Low energy availability is best described as insufficient energy remaining for normal physiological function after accounting for exercise expenditure. Which consequence may follow?
options: Improved immunity in every athlete
Health and performance disturbance across several body systems
Permanent protection from bone stress injury
An automatic increase in muscle glycogen
explanation: Low energy availability can affect endocrine, bone, immune, metabolic and psychological health and may impair performance.

text: What is the main purpose of random allocation in a controlled trial?
options: To remove the need for outcome measurement
To guarantee that every participant improves
To balance known and unknown factors between groups on average
To ensure the intervention is cheaper
explanation: Randomisation helps distribute prognostic factors between groups and reduces selection bias, although it does not guarantee perfect balance in a small sample.

text: Which nutrition strategy generally supports muscle repair during rehabilitation?
options: Avoid all protein until soreness disappears
Consume carbohydrate alone after every session
Replace meals with untested supplements
Distribute adequate high-quality protein across meals
explanation: Adequate protein distributed across the day supports muscle protein remodelling, alongside sufficient total energy and other nutrients.

text: Which initial examination priority best fits this presentation?
options: Check fracture indicators and neurovascular status before loading the ankle
Begin maximal hopping to identify the weakest direction
Clear the athlete because swelling is expected after all sprains
Test only hip strength and ignore the injured region
explanation: Acute ankle assessment should first consider fracture risk, neurovascular status, swelling, range and the athlete's ability to bear weight.
passage: A basketball player lands on another player's foot. There is lateral ankle swelling and pain with weight bearing, but the foot is warm with normal sensation. The athlete wants to return for the second half.

text: If fracture screening is negative and weight bearing is possible, which early intervention is most appropriate?
options: Complete bed rest for two weeks
Protected progressive loading with symptom-guided range and strength work
Immediate maximal cutting drills
Repeated painful inversion stretching
explanation: Early protected movement and progressive loading are generally preferred to prolonged complete rest when serious injury has been excluded.
passage: A basketball player lands on another player's foot. There is lateral ankle swelling and pain with weight bearing, but the foot is warm with normal sensation. The athlete wants to return for the second half.

text: Which finding would be most useful before considering return to unrestricted court movement?
options: A single pain-free passive movement performed while seated
A promise that the ankle will not swell again
The athlete's ability to tolerate sport-specific hopping, cutting and landing without a concerning response
The number of days since the injury alone
explanation: Return decisions should include function and sport-specific load tolerance, not only time since injury or one passive test.
passage: A basketball player lands on another player's foot. There is lateral ankle swelling and pain with weight bearing, but the foot is warm with normal sensation. The athlete wants to return for the second half.

text: The athlete asks why a brace may be used during early return. Which answer is best?
options: It guarantees that another sprain cannot occur
It replaces the need for balance and strength rehabilitation
It makes pain and swelling clinically irrelevant
It can provide external support while the athlete rebuilds capacity
explanation: External support may reduce stress or improve confidence during activity, but it complements rather than replaces rehabilitation.
passage: A basketball player lands on another player's foot. There is lateral ankle swelling and pain with weight bearing, but the foot is warm with normal sensation. The athlete wants to return for the second half.

text: What is the most important first question after this shoulder event?
options: Whether there was a deformity, neurovascular symptom or reduction event
Whether the athlete can immediately perform a maximal bench press
Whether the athlete has changed running shoes
Whether the athlete can hold a plank for two minutes
explanation: A traumatic shoulder event requires assessment of deformity, reduction history, circulation and nerve function before routine rehabilitation decisions.
passage: A volleyball player falls on an abducted, externally rotated arm. The shoulder was briefly deformed and reduced on the court. The athlete now reports tingling over the lateral shoulder and wants to continue.

text: Tingling over the lateral shoulder after an anterior dislocation raises concern about which nerve?
options: Median nerve
Axillary nerve
Ulnar nerve
Tibial nerve
explanation: The axillary nerve can be affected during anterior shoulder dislocation and should be checked with sensation and deltoid function.
passage: A volleyball player falls on an abducted, externally rotated arm. The shoulder was briefly deformed and reduced on the court. The athlete now reports tingling over the lateral shoulder and wants to continue.

text: Which next step is most appropriate before planning sport-specific strengthening?
options: Ignore the neurological symptom because the joint is reduced
Start aggressive end-range external rotation loading
Arrange medical assessment and document neurovascular findings
Clear the athlete if passive range is nearly normal
explanation: Neurological symptoms after dislocation warrant documented neurovascular assessment and appropriate medical review before progression.
passage: A volleyball player falls on an abducted, externally rotated arm. The shoulder was briefly deformed and reduced on the court. The athlete now reports tingling over the lateral shoulder and wants to continue.

text: When return training eventually begins, which principle is safest?
options: Rely on the athlete's desire to play as the only clearance criterion
Use only passive range until the season ends
Test the most provocative position first at maximal speed
Progress range, strength, control and sport exposure according to criteria
explanation: Return should progress the relevant physical and sport demands using symptoms, examination findings, control and shared decision-making.
passage: A volleyball player falls on an abducted, externally rotated arm. The shoulder was briefly deformed and reduced on the court. The athlete now reports tingling over the lateral shoulder and wants to continue.

text: Which examination finding would support an adductor-related groin pain classification?
options: Pain reproduced with resisted adduction and adductor palpation
Pain only with resisted wrist extension
Isolated numbness in the thumb
Tenderness over the lateral ankle alone
explanation: The Doha agreement uses the patient's reported pain location and clinical examination findings such as pain on resisted adduction and adductor palpation.
